what_its_for: Lurasidone is used to treat schizophrenia (a mental health condition that affects how you think, feel, and behave) and bipolar depression (episodes of sadness and low mood linked to bipolar disorder). It helps balance certain chemicals in your brain to improve your mood, thinking, and behavior.
how_to_take: Take lurasidone by mouth, once a day, WITH a meal. Your meal should have at least 350 calories. Taking it with food helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. The usual starting dose is 40 mg once daily for schizophrenia and 20 mg once daily for bipolar depression. Your doctor may slowly adjust your dose based on how you respond and any side effects you have. The maximum dose is usually 160 mg per day for schizophrenia and 120 mg per day for bipolar depression. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if you still have more than 12 hours before your next scheduled dose. If it is less than 12 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store lurasidone tablets at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication past its expiration date. If you need to dispose of unused medicine, ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking grapefruit juice or eating grapefruit while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of lurasidone in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Be careful driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated — drink plenty of fluids, especially in hot weather or during exercise. Tell your doctor before taking any other medications, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, as some medicines can interact with lurasidone.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body; high fever, stiff muscles, confusion, or irregular heartbeat (signs of a serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome); feeling faint or having a very fast or irregular heartbeat; severe dizziness when standing up; thoughts of harming yourself or others; unusual weight gain; increased blood sugar (increased thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision); difficulty swallowing; signs of infection such as fever or chills; rash or allergic reaction (swelling of face, lips, throat, or tongue). Also contact your doctor if your symptoms worsen or you do not feel better after a few weeks.
when_it_works: Lurasidone does not work right away. You may start to notice some improvement in sleep, appetite, and energy within the first 1 to 2 weeks. However, it may take 4 to 6 weeks or longer to feel the full benefit of this medication. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you do not notice improvement right away. Do not stop taking lurasidone without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can make your condition worse.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older): Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness, falls, and confusion. This medicine is not approved for treating dementia-related behavior problems in elderly patients, as it may increase the risk of serious side effects. Pregnant women: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who took antipsychotics in the last trimester of pregnancy may experience withdrawal symptoms or movement problems after birth. Breastfeeding: It is not known if lurasidone passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding. Children and teenagers: Lurasidone is approved for children aged 13 to 17 for schizophrenia and aged 10 to 17 for bipolar depression. The dose for children is adjusted based on weight and the condition being treated. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more carefully if you have kidney or liver disease.
